steps.body:
Meeting a part is only half the work.

Jung called the next step 'Education' — not schooling, but bringing what you understood down into how you actually live. Insight that stays in imagination doesn't transform behavior. It needs a point of contact with reality.

This is that point.

steps.title: What came up in your last meeting — or in recent work?
steps.body: A part, a quality, something you recognized. Briefly. Just enough to locate yourself.

The strongest intentions name the moment in advance.

Not 'I'll be braver' — but 'Next time this exact thing happens, I will do that.' You're deciding ahead of time, so when the old reflex shows up, it doesn't get the only vote.

It works because you've already chosen.

steps.title: Write it as a plan: Next time ___, I will ___.
steps.body: Name the trigger and the small action together. One moment, one choice where this insight gets to live. Keep it small enough that you'll actually do it.
steps.placeholder: Next time I feel the urge to shrink in a meeting, I will say one sentence before I talk myself out of it.

steps.title: What's the most likely way this doesn't happen?
steps.body: Naming the obstacle isn't pessimism — it's preparation.
steps.placeholder: What will pull you back toward the familiar…

exit.body: Your plan is saved in the Reflections tab. The distance between insight and living it closes one act at a time.
